First slice is LOCKED by PO. Please draft testable acceptance criteria — I'll fold them into the spec doc I'm writing now.

## Slice: "Lay out the rehearsal schedule" (conductor/admin-first)
End-to-end flow: create season → create recurring rehearsal `event_series` → BFF eagerly generates `event` instances → conductor views the rehearsal list → cancel/edit a single instance.

## In-scope capabilities — need AC for each
1. **Create season** — name, start_date, end_date, description(opt); date validation (end ≥ start); admin (`_owner` on org). *(extends existing #19 ADMIN-1 — reconcile, don't duplicate)*
2. **Create rehearsal series** — name, event_type=rehearsal, interval_days, start_time, duration_minutes, start_date, end_date, default_location(opt); must sit under the season; conductor (`_editor`). *(extends #20 ADMIN-2's series half)*
3. **Generate event instances (eager)** — on series save, BFF creates one `event` per occurrence from start_date stepping by interval_days through end_date, at start_time, duration inherited. Each event parented to org+season+series. AC for: correct count, correct dates/times, inheritance of unset fields. *(NEW — no issue exists)*
4. **View generated rehearsal list** — conductor sees the rehearsals (chronological); this is the "primary screen they live in" you flagged as the gap. AC for: list shows date/time/location, grouped or labelled by series. *(NEW)*
5. **Cancel / edit a single instance** — delete one rehearsal (others untouched); edit one instance's fields (override inherited). AC for: single-delete leaves siblings intact; edited instance keeps its overrides. *(NEW)*

## Explicitly OUT (do NOT write AC): concerts/programs, repertoire, RSVP, attendance, editing the series PATTERN after creation (regeneration), section-scoping, public/private visibility toggles.

## Notes
- Keep AC testable + specific (Given/When/Then or numbered assertions).
- Flag which existing issues (#19, #20) this satisfies vs extends, and whether we should file NEW issues for capabilities 3/4/5 (the attendance-style gaps you found). Recommend; I decide + file.
- Bentham is vetting the rights/data model in parallel — if his verdict changes anything I'll relay it before you finalize.

Send the AC back to me as structured markdown. Thanks Vic.

[2026-05-31 23:56]

All three are real — thank you. Decisions so you're unblocked; I'll fold them into the spec myself (keeping it coherent) alongside Bentham's pending Cap-7 verdict, in one pass.

**Gap 1 (direct-vs-inherited grant distinction):** Agree — this is the same mechanics uncertainty I flagged to Bentham. Expanding **probe #4** to: "confirm GET on the season's rights view separates DIRECT `_editor` grants from INHERITED/cascaded org-owner rights." If the API returns a flat merged set, item-5 "list conductors" needs a rethink — so this becomes a gating probe, not a nice-to-have. Good catch.

**Gap 2 (unassign → already-created events): DECISION = your option (A).** Unassign removes the season `_editor` grant + its cascade (ability to create/edit NEW under the season). Any residual entity-level rights the conductor holds on series/events they personally created are left as-is — **accepted v1 state, documented explicitly.** Option (B) (cascade-revoke entity-level grants) is expensive + risky + out of slice-1 spirit. BUT note: whether the creator even auto-gets entity-level `_owner` on what they create is an **unverified Entu mechanic** — I'm adding it to probe #4 too ("does creating an entity auto-grant the creator `_owner` on it?"). If creators DON'T auto-get owner, the cascade revoke is total and the gap vanishes. Either way (A) is the documented behavior.

**Gap 3 (display-name resolution):** Agree — making it explicit, matching your ADMIN-5 wording: "BFF resolves each grantee's display name via a separate `GET /entity/{personId}` (single-hop; not formula-traversable, per v4E rule)."

No need to draft — I'll edit the spec. You'll see the consolidated version; flag anything off. Still holding on `gh issue` until PO approves + Bentham GREENs Cap 7. Thanks Vic — sharp pass.
